codeReview.summary: The new `ValueError` path does catch fully unsupported requests like `alpaca/K`, but the guard rail is implemented as an all-or-nothing `if not hmms` check after the full load loop. That means explicit requests that mix supported and unsupported species/chain pairs still silently drop the unsupported pair instead of raising the descriptive error promised by the feature.

issues.description: The guard rail only runs when `not hmms`, so it misses explicit requests that contain at least one supported pair alongside an unsupported one. Reproduced from the reviewed code with `Renumbering(allowed_species=['alpaca'], allowed_chain=['H', 'K'], run_multiproc=False)`, which returns only `alpaca_H` without raising, and with `Renumbering(allowed_species=['human', 'alpaca'], allowed_chain=['K'], run_multiproc=False)`, which returns only `human_K`. In both cases an explicitly requested unsupported combo is still silently skipped, which does not satisfy the feature requirement to raise when a requested species/chain combination has no HMM.

The new guard-rail tests only cover requests where every requested pair is unsupported (`alpaca/K`, `alpaca/L`, `chicken/K`). There is no regression test for mixed explicit requests such as `['alpaca'] x ['H', 'K']` or `['human', 'alpaca'] x ['K']`, so the narrowed `if not hmms` implementation gap is left untested.
